hypotheses.justification:
The current proof uses `hC` (through `singularFactor_one_le` and `singularFactor_nat_moment`), but the statement stays true for every real `C`, and a proof can reuse the file's own `divisor_product_mean`.

Pointwise bound. Let j be in Ioc 0 U. Mathlib's `Real.abs_rpow_le_abs_rpow` gives Σ(j)^r ≤ |Σ(j)|^r, and it also covers negative bases, where x^r = exp(log x · r)·cos(rπ). Since |Σ(j)| = ∏_{p∣j} |1 + C/p| (by `Finset.abs_prod`) and every factor is nonnegative, |Σ(j)|^r = ∏_{p∣j} g(p) with g(p) = |1 + C/p|^r ≥ 0 (by `Real.finset_prod_rpow`). Let b_p = max(g(p) − 1, 0) ≥ 0. Then g(p) ≤ 1 + b_p, so Σ(j)^r ≤ ∏_{p ∈ primesLE U} (if p ∣ j then 1 + b_p else 1). This is the same rewriting as `heq` in `singularFactor_nat_moment`.

Degenerate cases. If some factor 1 + C/p is 0, then Σ(j) = 0 and 0^r ≤ 1 (`Real.zero_rpow_le_one`), so the bound still holds. If r = 0, every term is 1.

Summing. `divisor_product_mean` only needs b ≥ 0 on the primes. It gives ∑_{j ≤ U} Σ(j)^r ≤ U · ∏_p (1 + b_p/p) ≤ U · exp(∑_p b_p/p).

Uniform bound on b_p. For primes p > 2|C|, the value 1 + C/p lies in [1/2, 3/2], and the map x ↦ x^r is Lipschitz there with some constant L depending on r. So b_p ≤ L|C|/p. Only finitely many primes satisfy p ≤ 2|C|, and for them b_p ≤ M for some constant M, so b_p ≤ 2|C|M/p. Hence b_p ≤ K'/p for all primes p, with K' independent of U.

Conclusion. ∑_p b_p/p ≤ K' ∑_p 1/p² ≤ K' (the file already proves this with `sum_reciprocal_square_tail`). So the statement holds with K = exp(K') > 0. Nothing else in the statement mentions `hC`, so it can be deleted on its own.
